set.descent_text: Reverse the last two traversing pitches until a ledge system leads toward the East Couloir, the gully at the toe of the ridge where the route began. A slung horn there allows a short rappel that skips an exposed fourth-class downclimb; alternatively, rappel from a tree to the col on the west side of the summit. The East Couloir is mostly third class with one short fourth-class step; early in the season it is full of snow, and later it is a loose gully.
set.approach: Take the unofficial climbers trail from the Jenny Lake west shore up the steep mouth of Hanging Canyon, passing Ribbon Cascade. Just under the falls beneath Arrowhead Pool, ford the creek onto the wide talus fan on the south side, with Cube Point overhead. Climbing begins at the lowest point of the ridge on its east end, right beside the East Couloir.

review.notes: Route page for start, couloir and approach; trip report for the horn rappel and the couloir's grade; East Ridge page for the Hanging Canyon trail.

set.descent_text: The usual way down is the Southwest Couloir, a loose gully on the south side of the spire that holds snow into early summer, so carry an axe then. The route can finish up Symmetry's east ridge or by joining the upper Direct Jensen pitches, and from the summit area you drop into the couloir.
set.approach: From the Jenny Lake area, follow the Cascade Canyon horse trail to the place where the broad Symmetry Couloir comes down from the south side of the spire. The ridge lies east of the Jensen Ridge and shares its approach. Begin at the broad wall right of the Jensen Ridge and work rightward around the nose of the Dietschy Ridge, then climb solid rock to the right of the crest.

review.notes: Route page gives approach (same as Jensen), finish options and the couloir descent; couloir character from its page.

set.descent_text: Scramble west from the top of the ridge toward the notch in the Southwest Ridge, where a rappel of about 75 ft goes down the west side, or continue to the summit first. The normal way down is the Southwest Couloir, a longer descent from here than from the Southwest Ridge. Slings on a tree help bypass a short fifth-class step in the couloir, and a wet fourth-class step near its foot is sometimes rappelled. Carry an axe in early season.
set.approach: From the Jenny Lake area, follow the Cascade Canyon horse trail to the place where the broad Symmetry Couloir comes down from the south side of the spire. The ridge forms the east wall of Templeton's Crack, the dark narrow couloir just before the Southwest Ridge. Climb the Symmetry Couloir on its climbers trail, descend into Templeton's Crack from where the Durrance Ridge begins, cross the gully and scramble the smooth slabs on the far side. A large square roof about a rope length up marks the line.

review.notes: Route page for start, notch rappel and descent; trip report for the approach, roof and rappel details.

set.descent_text: Above the top of the ridge, a bowl to the left leads up to a notch high on the Southwest Ridge. There you can continue to the summit or descend: a single rappel of roughly 75 ft from the rap station drops west into the top of the Southwest Couloir, which is then a loose gully back to the horse trail. In early season the couloir is snow and the ledges above it can hold wet slop, so slow downclimbing and an axe are worth having.
set.approach: From the Jenny Lake area, follow the Cascade Canyon horse trail to the place where the broad Symmetry Couloir comes down from the south side of the spire. Go up the couloir beyond Templeton's Crack and the cliffs beside it, then cross the wooded slope sideways to where the ridge begins, over the talus and cliffs under that crack. A climbers trail on the north side of the main drainage is easier than the drainage itself; carry an axe in early season.

review.notes: Route page for bowl, notch and approach; trip reports for the rap station into the couloir, the trail line and early-season state.

set.descent_text: The usual way down is the Southwest Couloir, a loose gully on the south side that holds snow in early season, so bring an axe if it does; the ridge can also be reversed. Both gaining the ridge and descending the couloir are among the harder parts of this class 4 route.
set.approach: Follow the unofficial trail from the northwest side of Jenny Lake past Ribbon Cascade into Hanging Canyon. Beyond the boulders at Arrowhead Pool, aim for the saddle that separates Symmetry Spire from Sam's Throne, the pinnacle just west of Cube Point. The ridge west of Sam's Throne can be gained by scrambling the rocks to the lowest trees.

review.notes: Route page for access and descent; Wikipedia for class 4 and Hanging Canyon access; trip report for the Jenny Lake trail.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes: three double-rope rappels from the rap station on the ledge near the dead tree at the end of the fourth pitch return to the base of the formation. Parties who continue to the summit face a long stretch of mostly fourth-class wandering, then take the climbers trail across ledges to the notch where the Southwest Couloir begins, which is the standard way off Symmetry. An axe is needed on early-season snow during the descent.
set.approach: Follow the Symmetry Couloir drainage about halfway up, traverse above the snow patch that lingers there (leave packs if going on to the summit), and ascend the obvious third- and fourth-class gully, a few hundred feet, to a hidden side canyon. Where the slope eases, angle up and left onto a ledge system. The route starts on broken third-class ledges about 70 m right of the first pitch of Reticent Slabs, at the right edge of the big roof.

review.notes: Incognito page, cross-checked with Reticent Slabs (same wall, same rappel line); couloir from its page.

set.descent_text: The standard way off Symmetry Spire is the Southwest Couloir, a loose gully on the south side; snow fills it into early summer, so bring an axe then.
set.approach: Take the unofficial trail from the Jenny Lake west shore past Ribbon Cascade into Hanging Canyon. Enter the canyon on its north side, north of the Symmetry Couloir, and head for the large chimney on the northeast side of the spire, between Arrowhead Pool and Ramshead Lake.

review.notes: Route page for location; East Ridge page for the Hanging Canyon trail; couloir page for the descent.

set.descent_text: Reverse the route, which is the normal way down for most climbs on the peak. Late in the season, the ledges on the northwest side of the upper couloir reduce rockfall exposure, and descending parties should stay on skier's right. In early season it is steep snow, and the stream below can be hidden under it, so avoid thin snow over the water, and remember the cliffs below if you glissade. By late summer it is rubble; a wet fourth-class step near the foot is sometimes rappelled.
set.approach: Near the top of the Cascade Canyon horse trail, on the east side of the creek that comes down the couloir, a faint climbers trail heads uphill to the north through sumac. It climbs a cliff band at a dry waterfall, follows ledges leftward, then crosses the stream. A fourth-class step in the lower gully can be wet and has an old fixed line that is best treated with caution.

review.notes: Route page for trail and hazards; trip reports for the wet step and the couloir as the descent.

set.descent_text: From the top of the arete, a sometimes exposed scramble of roughly 400 ft leads east toward the summit. Before the summit block there is a large notch above the descent route; a single-rope rappel west from here drops into the Southwest Couloir, and the descent continues down that loose gully. Take the rappel station at the notch if the weather turns.
set.approach: From the Jenny Lake area, follow the Cascade Canyon horse trail to the place where the broad Symmetry Couloir comes down from the south side of the spire. A faint, brushy climbers trail climbs away from the horse trail on the left, about 20 ft beyond a rocky runoff. The route follows the arete at the point where the Symmetry Couloir curves rightward, and parties tie in by a few trees at its foot. The approach and descent through the loose couloir take much longer than the distance suggests.

review.notes: Route page for notch, rappel and approach; trip reports for the rappel station.

set.descent_text: Downclimb the route. Rappels are not advised on the upper section because the rock is loose and low-angle. The ledges near the top are fourth class and exposed, and the snow below is steep enough that a fall could be fatal, so an axe and crampons are standard. The Southwest Couloir on the south side is the peak's usual way down if you prefer not to reverse this line.
set.approach: Take the unofficial trail into Hanging Canyon past Ribbon Cascade and Arrowhead Pool, then continue to Ramshead Lake. The route climbs the couloir above the stream that links Ramshead Lake to Lake of the Crags, on moderately steep snow to the col that divides the northwest and southeast couloirs.

review.notes: Route page for downclimb and snow; East Ridge page for the trail; couloir page for the alternate descent.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route using two ropes: three double-rope rappels start from the slings on the large dead tree near the top of the fourth pitch, and return to the base. If you continue to the summit, a chossy fifth-class weakness leads to a ledge system, then a ridge scramble. From near the top, traverse north on the climbers trail over exposed ledges to the notch at the head of the Southwest Couloir, then go down that loose gully. Bring an axe for early-season snow.
set.approach: Follow the Symmetry Couloir drainage about halfway up, traverse above the persistent snow patch (leave packs here if heading for the summit) and ascend the obvious third- and fourth-class gully, a few hundred feet, to a hidden side canyon. Where the slope eases, angle up and left onto a ledge system with trees. Start beneath the big roof and flakes of the first pitch. Later in the season the moat in the snow patch is easier to follow.

review.notes: Route page; same wall and rappels cross-checked on Incognito Buttress.

set.descent_text: Several fourth-class lines lead down the north side, or you can use a short rappel off a fixed anchor; either way you end up in Hanging Canyon below the tower. From there the Hanging Canyon trail past Ribbon Cascade leads out toward Jenny Lake. The tower is the spire that stands in the gap separating Cube Point from Symmetry's East Ridge.

review.notes: Route page for north-side descent and location; approach left out because no source says how to reach the start notch.

wy_reticent_wall.skip_reason: no route page found for Reticent Wall; it appears only as the wall that Reticent Slabs and Incognito Buttress finish on, so its line and top-out cannot be placed
